PC:
Physician in team must:
Recognize ventricular fibrillation on monitor
Order CPR including ventilations via bag-valve-mask
Order defibrillation at appropriate voltage
Order epinephrine
Order amioderone, lidocaine, or procainamaide
Repeat defibrillation
Recognize unresponsive patient after ROSC (return of spontaneous circulation) and proceed with intubation

Nurses in team must:
Establish IV access.
Put patient on monitor
Call out vital signs and monitor readings
Administer medications
Administer defibrillation

EMTs and other support staff must:
Begin CPR at appropriate rate and technique
Proceed with ventilation with appropriate technique
SBP: Situational Awareness by all members of staff- recognition of progression of care.
Decision Making- Leaders guide care (defibrillation, intubation) but other members of team are involved (starting IVs without specific orders).
Transition of leadership from the physician to another team member as the physician turns focus to the family

Recognition of the patient’s return to an unstable state while the physician is talking to the family, and action by the team members to reinitiate ACLS or, at a minimum, inform the physician of the changed status.
Flexibility of decision making- ability of all members of the team to change clinical path during resuscitation after family arrives
ICS: Call-outs and check backs when orders are ordered and performed

Acknowledge and validate other’s feelings – the natural reaction is to defend the course of care (“This is what we do when we do not know.”), which does nothing to validate the family’s feelings. Instead we look for a reaction such as, “If this is not what your mother wanted, we can certainly understand why you are so upset.”
Focus on the problem-not the person
Gain agreement on one of the option’s presented
